2366-the-beldonald-holbein.title: The Beldonald Holbein
2366-the-beldonald-holbein.creator: Henry James
2366-the-beldonald-holbein.description: A book by Henry James. Munden in a manner corrected me, but it _was_ difficult to express. "My brother at all events was certainly selfish. Till he died she was almost never in London; they wintered, year after year, for what he supposed to be his health--which it didn't help, since he was so much too soon to meet his end--in the south of France and in the dullest holes he could pick out, and when they came back to England he always kept her in the country.

arxiv-1911-01895.title: On notions of compactness, object classifiers and weak Tarski universes
arxiv-1911-01895.creator: Raffael Stenzel
arxiv-1911-01895.description: Abstract We prove a correspondence between κ \kappa -small fibrations in simplicial presheaf categories equipped with the injective or projective model structure (and left Bousfield localizations thereof) and relatively κ \kappa -compact maps in their underlying quasi-categories for suitably large regular cardinals κ \kappa .

arxiv-2012-03278.title: Band gaps of crystalline solids from Wannier-localization based optimal tuning of a screened range-separated hybrid functional DOI: www.pnas.org/cgi/doi/10.1073/pnas.XXXXXXXXXX
arxiv-2012-03278.creator: Dahvyd Wing, Guy Ohad, Jonah B. Haber, Marina R. Filip, Stephen E. Gant, Jeffrey B. Neaton, Leeor Kronik
arxiv-2012-03278.description: Abstract Accurate prediction of fundamental band gaps of crystalline solid state systems entirely within density functional theory is a long standing challenge. Here, we present a simple and inexpensive method that achieves this by means of non-empirical optimal tuning of the parameters of a screened range-separated hybrid functional.

arxiv-2207-09247.title: The differential structure of generators of GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroups
arxiv-2207-09247.creator: Melchior Wirth
arxiv-2207-09247.description: Abstract . We show that the generator of a GNS-symmetric quantum Markov semigroup can be written as the square of a derivation. This generalizes a result of Cipriani and Sauvageot for tracially symmetric semigroups. Compared to the tracially symmetric case, the derivations in the general case satisfy a twisted product rule, reflecting the non-triviality of their modular group.

arxiv-2211-01130.title: Unimodular gravity and the gauge/gravity duality
arxiv-2211-01130.creator: Jesus Anero
arxiv-2211-01130.description: Abstract Unimodular gravity can be formulated so that transverse diffeomorphisms and Weyl transformations are symmetries of the theory. For this formulation of unimodular gravity, we work out the two-point and three-point h μ ​ ν h_{\mu\nu} contributions to the on-shell classical gravity action in the leading approximation and for an Euclidean AdS background.

arxiv-2312-13603.title: Style modeling for Multi-Speaker Articulation-to-Speech
arxiv-2312-13603.creator: Miseul Kim, Zhenyu Piao, Jihyun Lee, Hong-Goo Kang
arxiv-2312-13603.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a neural articulation-to-speech (ATS) framework that synthesizes high-quality speech from articulatory signal in a multi-speaker situation. Most conventional ATS approaches only focus on modeling contextual information of speech from a single speaker’s articulatory features.

arxiv-2401-05423.title: Introduction of L0 norm and application of L1 and C1 norm in the study of time-series of indices of cryptocurrencies, South American currencies, banking indices and European indices.
arxiv-2401-05423.creator: Víctor Ujaldón García
arxiv-2401-05423.description: Abstract Four markets are considered: Cryptocurrencies / South American exchange rate / Spanish Banking indices and European Indices and studied using TDA (Topological Data Analysis) tools. These tools are used to predict and showcase both strengths and weakness of the current TDA tools.

arxiv-2410-02051.title: TESS Asteroseismic Masses and Radii of Red Giants with (and without) Planets
arxiv-2410-02051.creator: Myles Pope, Joleen K. Carlberg, Jeff Valenti, Doug Branton
arxiv-2410-02051.description: Abstract We present a study of asteroseismically derived surface gravities, masses, and radii of a sample of red giant stars both with and without confirmed planetary companions using TESS photometric light curves. These red giants were drawn from radial velocity surveys, and their reported properties in the literature rely on more traditional methods using spectroscopy and isochrone fitting.

arxiv-2411-06955.title: Optical orthogonal codes from a combinatorial perspective
arxiv-2411-06955.creator: Sophie Huczynska, Siaw-Lynn Ng
arxiv-2411-06955.description: Abstract Optical orthogonal codes (OOCs) are sets of ( 0 , 1 ) (0,1) -sequences with good auto- and cross- correlation properties. They were originally introduced for use in multi-access communication, particularly in the setting of optical CDMA communications systems.

arxiv-2503-05529.title: PoSSUM: A P r o tocol for S urveying S ocial-media U sers with M ultimodal LLMs
arxiv-2503-05529.creator: Roberto Cerina
arxiv-2503-05529.description: Abstract This paper introduces PoSSUM , an open-source protocol for unobtrusive polling of social-media users via multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs). PoSSUM leverages users’ real-time posts, images, and other digital traces to create silicon samples that capture information not present in the LLM’s training data.

arxiv-2504-10906.title: Understanding LLMs’ Cross-Lingual Context Retrieval: How Good It Is And Where It Comes From Thanks: Corresponding author
arxiv-2504-10906.creator: Changjiang Gao ♣ \clubsuit, Hankun Lin ♣ \clubsuit, Xin Huang ◇ \Diamond
arxiv-2504-10906.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Changjiang Gao ♣ \clubsuit, Hankun Lin ♣ \clubsuit, Xin Huang ◇ \Diamond. Cross-lingual context retrieval (extracting contextual information in one language based on requests in another) is a fundamental aspect of cross-lingual alignment, but the performance and mechanism of it for large language models (LLMs) remains unclear. In this paper, we evaluate the cross-lingual context retrieval of over 40 LLMs across 12 languages, using cross-lingual machine reading comprehension (xMRC) as a representative scenario.

arxiv-2505-03666.title: A Centrality-independent Framework for Revealing Genuine Higher-Order Cumulants in Heavy-Ion Collisions
arxiv-2505-03666.creator: Zhaohui Wang, Xiaofeng Luo
arxiv-2505-03666.description: Abstract We propose a novel centrality definition-independent method for analyzing higher-order cumulants, specifically addressing the challenge of volume fluctuations that dominate in low-energy heavy-ion collisions. This method reconstructs particle number distributions using the Edgeworth expansion, with parameters optimized via a combination of differential evolution algorithm and Bayesian inference.

arxiv-2505-14688.title: Semi-Competitive Differential Game Logic
arxiv-2505-14688.creator: Julia Butte, André Platzer
arxiv-2505-14688.description: Abstract This paper introduces semi-competitive differential game logic dG ℒ s ​ c \mathcal{L}_{sc} , which enables verification of safety-critical applications that involve interactions between two agents. In dG ℒ s ​ c \mathcal{L}_{sc} , these interactions are specified as games on hybrid systems with two players that may collaborate with each other when helpful and may compete when necessary.

arxiv-2506-11129.title: Trustworthy AI for Medicine: Continuous Hallucination Detection and Elimination with CHECK
arxiv-2506-11129.creator: Carlos Garcia-Fernandez, Luis Felipe, Monique Shotande, Muntasir Zitu, Aakash Tripathi, Ghulam Rasool, Issam El Naqa, Vivek Rudrapatna, Gilmer Valdes
arxiv-2506-11129.description: Abstract “If you tell the truth you don’t have to remember anything.” — Mark Twain Abstract Large language models (LLMs) show promise in healthcare, but hallucinations remain a major barrier to clinical use. We present CHECK, a continuous-learning framework that integrates structured clinical databases with a classifier grounded in information theory to detect both factual and reasoning-based hallucinations.

pmc-11466954.description: The antibody response to vaccination and infection is a key component of the immune response to pathogens. Sequencing of peripheral B cells may not represent the complete B cell receptor repertoire. Here we present a method for sequencing human plasma-derived polyclonal IgG using a combination of mass spectrometry and B-cell sequencing.

pmc-11497042.title: Sirtuin 5‐Mediated Desuccinylation of ALDH2 Alleviates Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress Following Acetaminophen‐Induced Acute Liver Injury
pmc-11497042.creator: Qiwen Yu, Jiakai Zhang, Jiye Li, Yaodong Song, Jie Pan, Chaopeng Mei, Mengwei Cui, Qianqian He, Haifeng Wang, Huihui Li, Bo Cheng, Yan Zhang, Wenzhi Guo, Changju Zhu, Sanyang Chen
pmc-11497042.description: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is a major cause of drug‐induced liver injury. Sirtuins 5 (SIRT5) has been implicated in the development of various liver diseases. However, its involvement in APAP‐induced acute liver injury (AILI) remains unclear. The present study aimed to explore the role of SIRT5 in AILI.

pmc-11715166.title: Medial temporal lobe subregional atrophy patterns in presymptomatic and symptomatic genetic frontotemporal lobar degeneration
pmc-11715166.creator: Leslie S Gaynor, Claire Yballa, Yann Cobigo, Jhony Alejandro Mejía‐Perez, Anika Wuestefeld, Laura EM Wisse, Leah K Forsberg, Hilary W Heuer, Howard J Rosen, Adam L Boxer, Brad F Boeve, Kejal Kantarci, Adam M Staffaroni, Renaud La Joie
pmc-11715166.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundMedial temporal lobe (MTL) atrophy is an early feature of multiple neurodegenerative diseases. In genetic frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD, i.e. individuals carrying GRN, MAPT, or C9orf72 mutations), MTL atrophy can occur 10‐15 years before symptom onset.

pmc-11805056.title: A Study on Patient Satisfaction and Prevalence of Complication on Surgical Extraction of Third Molar
pmc-11805056.creator: Ahtesham Ahmad Qurishi, Amal Bajonaid, Maryam H. Mugri, Husham E. Homeida, Ogail Yousif Dawod, Haider Hussain Alhijji, Albaraa Abeid Dayili
pmc-11805056.description: Introduction:The surgical extraction of third molars is a common procedure often accompanied by various complications. This study evaluates patient satisfaction and the prevalence of complications to identify factors influencing postoperative outcomes.Methodology:A cross-sectional study was conducted with 62 patients who underwent third molar extraction. Data on demographics, complications, and patient satisfaction were collected through medical records and structured questionnaires.

pmc-12386811.creator: Beata Donarska, Klaudia Seklecka, Joanna Cytarska, Katarzyna Piechowska, Przemyslaw Ledwon, Sławomir Kula, Przemysław Krawczyk, Angelika Baranowska-Łączkowska, Krzysztof Z. Łączkowski
pmc-12386811.description: This presented study depicts the synthesis of three novel carbazole–thiazole conjugates, thoroughly investigating their spectroscopic properties as well as evaluating their biological activity as tyrosinase inhibitors. Additionally, we investigated the possibility of using Concanavalin A (ConA) complexes with dyes from a theoretical point of view, developing a promising protein-based strategy of delivery of dyes to the target cells.

uslaw-usc-t7-s1738b.description: United States Code, Title 7 (Agriculture); Chapter 41 (Food For Peace); Subchapter VI (Enterprise For The Americas Initiative). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Requirements To be eligible for benefits from the Facility under this subchapter, a country shall— (1) be a Latin American or Caribbean country; (2) have in effect or have received approval for, or, as appropriate in exceptional circumstances.
